chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ubayd ibn Abi Abdillah Al-Baghdadi, from the one who informed him, said:

A guest lodged with Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and was seated in his presence discussing with him during one of the nights. So the lantern dimmed, and the man extended his hand to correct it. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) stopped him, then attended to it himself, so he corrected it. Then he said to him: 'We are a people who do not make our guests serve.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding hosts and guests serving each other?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) personally trimmed the lamp for a guest, demonstrating the Ahl al-Bayt's practice of elevating the guest's status through humble service rather than expecting service. This act underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the spiritual merit of hosting, where the host serves the guest to honor them, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of generosity. The incident serves as a practical model for distinguishing between mere hospitality and the elevated etiquette of the Imams.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, from Ubeyd Bin Abu Abdullah Al Baghdady, from the one who informed him, said,

‘A guest had lodge with Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, and was seated in his<sup>asws</sup> presence discussing with him<sup>asws</sup> in one of the nights. So the lantern dimmed, and the man extended his hand to correct it. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> stopped him, then attended to it himself<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> corrected it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> are a people who do not make our<sup>asws</sup> gests to serve’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from al-Sayyariy from ‘Ubayd ibn abu ‘Abd Allah al-Baghdadiy from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “

Once abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’ ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had a guest who was sitting with him (the Imam) and speaking during the night. The lamp began to become dim and the man stretched his hand to repair it. Abu al-Hassan, stopped him seriously and he (the Imam) himself repaired the lamp saying, ‘We are a people who do not make the guests work.’”
